key_insight: Tuning inter-nanoparticle repulsion produces four morphologies—droplet, slab, crystalline droplet, and dispersed—with distinct effects on polymer ordering.
engineering_relevance: Interparticle repulsion offers a design lever for controlling nanoparticle dispersion and polymer organization in strongly confined polymer nanocomposites.
method: Run Langevin dynamics simulations under extreme confinement.
Vary nanoparticle repulsion while holding other interactions fixed.
Analyze nanoparticle clusters, crystallinity, and polymer nematic order.
evidence_signal: Structural analyses identify the strongest polymer nematic ordering in the weakly crystalline slab regime, reduced nematic order around crystalline droplets, and local smectic-like ordering in the dispersed regime.
watch_item: Results concern an extremely confined model with semiflexible, rod-like polymers; applicability to bulk composites and experimental systems remains to be established.
paper_title: Inter-Nanoparticle Repulsion Effect on Self-Organization in Polymer Nanocomposites: A Langevin Dynamics Simulation Study
